newsitem.title: USA: H.B. Fuller gains boost fiscal Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: H.B. Fuller gains boost fiscal Q2 results.

text.p: H.B. Fuller Co, a manufacturer of sealants, adhesives and coatings, said Wednesday that improved volume growth, higher gross margins and strong control of operating expenses boosted fiscal 1997 second quarter results.
Earlier, the specialty chemical company reported a 32 percent increase in net earnings and a 31 percent increase in earnings per share for its second quarter ending May 31, 1997.

Fiscal 1997 second quarter sales rose 2.7 percent from the year ago quarter to $328.9 million. Year-ago second quarter sales included $7.2 million from the Monarch Division, which was divested later in the year. Excluding those sales from the year-ago total, the company's comparable sales in the second quarter of 1997 increased 5.1 percent.

Sales of North American operations in the second quarter rose five percent from last year. A 1996 acquisition and an 1997 automotive joint venture contributed another three percentage points. The divestiture of the Monarch Division had a negative four percentage point impact.

The company's European operations reported an eight percent decrease in sales for the second quarter compared to the prior-year period. Pricing and a strengthening U.S. dollar, combined, had a negative 13 percentage point impact on those sales and the divestiture of a construction business had a negative three percentage point impact.

Latin American operations had a two percent increase in sales in the second quarter compared to the prior year. Operating earnings increased slightly from the prior year's second quarter, primarily due to better gross margins.
Asia/Pacific sales for the quarter increased 13 percentage points over prior year.
